title: Colorado Springs Home Rebates 2026: Springs Utilities Heat Pump, Water Heater and Insulation
desc: Colorado Springs home rebates for 2026 from Colorado Springs Utilities: $1,500 to $3,000 for heat pumps, $750 for a heat pump water heater, 40% for insulation, and thermostat rewards.
badge: $1,500 to $3,000 for a heat pump from Springs Utilities
lead: In Colorado Springs, the utility that sends your bill is the rebate office. Colorado Springs Utilities sells electricity, gas and water, and in 2026 it pays for heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, insulation and smart thermostats. It pays for efficient gas equipment too.
cards_heading: What is open for Colorado Springs homes in 2026
cards_intro: We read Colorado Springs Utilities' 2026 rebate form, its HVAC and water heater pages and its rebate rules on October 5, 2026. Everything on it is post-purchase: buy and install in 2026, then apply by January 31, 2027. Rebates are first come, first served.

cards.title: Heat pump (cold-climate, 3 tons and over)
cards.note: NEEP certified. Cold-climate units under 3 tons and ENERGY STAR heat pumps pay $1,500. Air-to-water heat pumps pay $3,000.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: For Colorado Springs Utilities electric customers, ENERGY STAR certified. A natural gas storage water heater pays $300 and a gas boiler $1,200.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: Attic (R-49 with bypass air sealing), wall (R-13) and crawl space (R-15 continuous). Colorado contractor required.

cards.title: Smart thermostat
cards.note: ENERGY STAR certified. Peak Energy Rewards adds $50 the first year and $25 a year after a full cooling season.

cards.title: State heat pump discount
cards.note: $83 for a heat pump water heater. Off your invoice from a registered contractor.

cards.title: State income-based rebates (HEAR)
cards.note: Up to $14,000 per household while open. El Paso County was in the Front Range region, now closed.

sections:
The American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) counts 211,353 homes in Colorado Springs. About 61% of households own and 39% rent. About 60% of homes are detached houses, the highest share of the five Colorado cities we cover. About 39% were built before 1980 and 30% in 2000 or later.

A city of single-family houses with a municipal utility suits a post-purchase rebate: one owner, one meter and one permit with the Pikes Peak Regional Building Department. Renters are 39% of households, so tenants should ask the owner about it.
Gas and electric from one utility

About 70% of Colorado Springs households heat with utility gas and 27% with electricity. Springs Utilities sells both, so it also pays $900 for a natural gas furnace and $1,200 for a gas boiler. A heat pump pays more, but compare running costs for your own house before you decide. The utility says it will also give a $1,500 electric bill credit to customers approved for a heat pump under three tons from January 1, 2026; see our heat pump page.
The rules that all the rebates share

Equipment must be bought and installed between January 1 and December 31 of the year, and the application postmarked by January 31 of the next. You need a receipt with the date, price, make, model and quantity, and for contractor work, the installer's information on company letterhead. Many measures need a permit and a final inspection with the Pikes Peak Regional Building Department. Rebates are credited to your account and can take up to eight weeks. Two rebates per address every three years apply to heat pumps, water heaters and thermostats.
What Colorado Springs does not have

The Xcel Energy rebates on our Denver page are not for Colorado Springs Utilities customers, and El Paso County is not on Power Ahead Colorado's county list. We did not find a Colorado Springs Utilities rebate for solar panels, batteries or EV chargers on its rebate pages, so we show none. Ask the utility directly before you buy those.

Our climate file, built from ten Januaries (2015 to 2024), shows an average January low of about 17°F and a coldest day near minus 25°F. The heat pump rebates ask for cold-climate (NEEP) models for the larger amounts.
claim_heading: How to claim Colorado Springs rebates
claim_steps: Confirm that Colorado Springs Utilities sends your electric and/or gas bill.
Read the rules for your measure on the utility's rules page, and keep the model number.
Hire a Colorado contractor, or do eligible work yourself with a Pikes Peak Regional Building Department permit.
Pass the final inspection and keep an itemized receipt.
Apply by email, mail or My Account, postmarked by January 31, 2027.
faq: What rebates can a Colorado Springs homeowner get in 2026?

From Colorado Springs Utilities: $1,500 to $3,000 for heat pumps, $750 for a heat pump water heater, 40% up to $1,250 for each insulation type, and up to $50 for a smart thermostat. The state also gives an invoice discount.
Is Xcel's rebate available in Colorado Springs?
No. Xcel's rebates are for Xcel customers.
Buy and install in 2026, then postmark your application by January 31, 2027.
Is there a rebate for solar or batteries?
We did not find one on Colorado Springs Utilities' rebate pages. Ask the utility before you buy.
Is the state's income-based program open?
No. The Colorado Energy Office says the single-family program is closed.
